rationale: Both candidates correctly recognize that the diff shown already incorporates fixes for the original enabler/partition and offline-example concerns, and both independently rediscover the same live residual bug (AsyncOmniEngine still hardcodes rel_l1_thresh=0.2, so the new None-sentinel/0.17 model default never reaches real serving) plus the reviewer's own noted gap that the E2E smoke test never asserts a cache hit occurred. X adds one uniquely valuable, well-evidenced finding (TeaCache/Cache-DiT can both get enabled for quality=='high', contradicting the PR's own 'mutually exclusive' doc claim), but its output is a dense, evidence-dump style that's harder to act on and includes some more speculative/hedged nits (AMD CI). Y is comparably grounded (cross-checks its default-threshold claim with actual executed values, verifies R² against the PR's own reported number) and is more precisely organized into blocking/should-fix/minor with concrete 'Change:' directives, plus it catches an additional clean, verifiable issue (the drive-by 39→107 frame edit silently changing the unrelated FP8 smoke test) that X misses.
